652: // ── Analytics stats cache (decay-weighted) ──────────────────────────────────
653: // Instead of the fork's flat 7-day window (where a model that degrades today
654: // keeps a stale week-long average), each request is weighted by an exponential
655: // decay so recent behavior dominates while older data still stabilizes the
656: // estimate. We aggregate by (model, integer day age) in SQL — at most ~7 rows
657: // per model — then apply the per-bucket decay weight in JS.
658: const WINDOW_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
659: const HALF_LIFE_DAYS = 2; // a 2-day-old request counts half as much as a fresh one
660: const CACHE_TTL_MS = 60 * 1000;
661: 
662: interface ModelStats {
663:   successes: number;   // decay-weighted pseudo-count
664:   failures: number;    // decay-weighted pseudo-count
665:   // Output tokens from successes over the time spent on successes AND timeouts
666:   // (#619 — see the accumulator below); 0 = no data.
667:   tokPerSec: number;
668:   avgTtfbMs: number | null; // null = no first-byte timing yet
669:   monthlyUsedTokens: number; // calendar-month usage, for the headroom guardrail
670:   // Decay-weighted requests that actually SAY something about speed: successes
671:   // plus timeouts. A model can have hundreds of 401s and still no speed signal,
672:   // so this — not successes + failures — is what gates the observed speed_rank
673:   // writeback.
674:   speedSamples: number;
675: }
676: 
677: // Per-key slice of the same window (#580): reliability/speed observed through
678: // ONE credential of a model. With unified groups, a model's traffic can span
679: // several keys whose real quality diverges (expired, quota-drained, region-
680: // blocked keys fail while siblings are fine) — the rolled-up model bucket
681: // can't see that, so key selection needs its own buckets.
682: interface KeyStats {
683:   successes: number;   // decay-weighted pseudo-count
684:   failures: number;    // decay-weighted pseudo-count
685:   tokPerSec: number;   // from successful requests only (0 = no data)
686:   avgTtfbMs: number | null;
687: }
688: 
689: // Keyed by modelStatsKey(): "platform:model_id" for catalog models, and
690: // "custom:model_id@base_url" for a relay model that carries an endpoint scope
691: // (#651). A single-endpoint install produces the same keys it always did.
692: let statsCache: Map<string, ModelStats> | null = null;
693: let keyStatsCache: Map<string, KeyStats> | null = null; // "platform:model_id:key_id"
694: let statsCacheTime = 0;
695: 
696: function decayWeight(ageDays: number): number {
697:   return Math.pow(0.5, Math.max(0, ageDays) / HALF_LIFE_DAYS);
698: }
699: 
700: // SQL predicate for "this row is a timed-out request" (#619). A timeout is an
701: // error row whose text carries one of the shared timeout markers
702: // (lib/error-classify.ts), which is also what the failover attempt trail
703: // classifies on. 'canceled' rows (#752 — client hung up) never reach this
704: // predicate: the stats query below filters them out entirely, because a
705: // vanished client says nothing about the model's reliability or speed. The
706: // markers are hard-coded lowercase identifiers from our own source, never
707: // user input, so interpolating them into the LIKE list is safe.
708: const IS_TIMEOUT_SQL = `(status != 'success' AND (${
709:   TIMEOUT_ERROR_MARKERS.map(m => `LOWER(COALESCE(error, '')) LIKE '%${m}%'`).join(' OR ')
710: }))`;
711: 
712: /** api_keys.id → endpoint scope, for every custom credential on record (#651). */
713: function customEndpointScopes(db: Db): Map<number, string> {
714:   const rows = db.prepare("SELECT id, base_url FROM api_keys WHERE platform = 'custom'")
715:     .all() as { id: number; base_url: string | null }[];
716:   return new Map(rows.map(r => [r.id, endpointScopeForBaseUrl(r.base_url)]));
717: }
718: 
719: export function refreshStatsCache(db: Db, force = false): void {
720:   if (!force && statsCache && Date.now() - statsCacheTime < CACHE_TTL_MS) return;
721: 
722:   // Re-read the community priors alongside the stats they season, so a forced
723:   // refresh (tests, admin actions) never routes on a stale prior snapshot.
724:   invalidateCommunityPriorCache();
725: 
726:   const since = new Date(Date.now() - WINDOW_MS).toISOString();
727:   // Grouped by (model, key, day age): still a handful of rows per model — key
728:   // count × ≤7 day buckets — so the finer grain keeps the same one-query,
729:   // 60s-cached shape. Aggregated two ways below: rolled up per model (ordering)
730:   // and per key (in-model key selection, #580).
731:   const buckets = db.prepare(`
732:     SELECT platform, model_id, key_id,
733:       CAST((julianday('now') - julianday(created_at)) AS INTEGER) AS age_days,
734:       COUNT(*) AS total,
735:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successes,
736:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'success' THEN output_tokens ELSE 0 END) AS succ_out,
737:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'success' THEN latency_ms ELSE 0 END) AS succ_lat,
738:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'success' AND ttfb_ms IS NOT NULL THEN ttfb_ms ELSE 0 END) AS succ_ttfb_sum,
739:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'success' AND ttfb_ms IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS succ_ttfb_cnt,
740:       SUM(CASE WHEN ${IS_TIMEOUT_SQL} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS timeouts,
741:       SUM(CASE WHEN ${IS_TIMEOUT_SQL} THEN MIN(MAX(latency_ms, 0), ${TIMEOUT_LATENCY_CAP_MS}) ELSE 0 END) AS timeout_lat
742:     FROM requests
743:     WHERE created_at >= ? AND status <> 'canceled'
744:     GROUP BY platform, model_id, key_id, age_days
745:   `).all(since) as Array<{
746:     platform: string; model_id: string; key_id: number | null; age_days: number; total: number; successes: number;
747:     succ_out: number; succ_lat: number; succ_ttfb_sum: number; succ_ttfb_cnt: number;
748:     timeouts: number; timeout_lat: number;
749:   }>;
750: 
751:   // Accumulate decay-weighted sums per model AND per key.
752:   //
753:   // Timeouts (#619) land in the SAME latency/TTFB accumulators as successes,
754:   // because that is what they are: time spent, nothing produced. Each one adds
755:   // its capped wall-clock latency to the throughput denominator with zero
756:   // output tokens, and that same figure as a first-byte sample — which is past
757:   // TTFB_WORST_MS, so it scores no latency credit. Net effect: a model that
758:   // times out constantly can no longer keep a stellar speed number just because
759:   // its handful of successes were quick.
760:   interface Acc { wSucc: number; wFail: number; wOut: number; wLat: number; wTtfbSum: number; wTtfbCnt: number; wTimeouts: number }
761:   const emptyAcc = (): Acc => ({ wSucc: 0, wFail: 0, wOut: 0, wLat: 0, wTtfbSum: 0, wTtfbCnt: 0, wTimeouts: 0 });
762:   const addBucket = (a: Acc, w: number, b: (typeof buckets)[number]): void => {
763:     a.wSucc += w * b.successes;
764:     a.wFail += w * (b.total - b.successes);
765:     a.wOut += w * b.succ_out;
766:     a.wLat += w * (b.succ_lat + b.timeout_lat);
767:     a.wTtfbSum += w * (b.succ_ttfb_sum + b.timeout_lat);
768:     a.wTtfbCnt += w * (b.succ_ttfb_cnt + b.timeouts);
769:     a.wTimeouts += w * b.timeouts;
770:   };
771:   // Which endpoint each custom credential belongs to, so a request logged
772:   // against relay A's key lands in relay A's bucket and nowhere else (#651).
773:   // `requests` has always recorded key_id, so pre-migration history splits
774:   // correctly too; rows whose key is gone (or that never had one) fall into the
775:   // un-scoped bucket, which only un-scoped rows read.
776:   const scopeByKeyId = customEndpointScopes(db);
777:   const scopeOf = (platform: string, keyId: number | null): string =>
778:     platform === 'custom' && keyId != null ? (scopeByKeyId.get(keyId) ?? '') : '';
779: 
780:   const acc = new Map<string, Acc>();
781:   const keyAcc = new Map<string, Acc>();
782:   for (const b of buckets) {
783:     const key = modelStatsKey(b.platform, b.model_id, scopeOf(b.platform, b.key_id));
784:     const w = decayWeight(b.age_days);
785:     let a = acc.get(key);
786:     if (!a) acc.set(key, a = emptyAcc());
787:     addBucket(a, w, b);
788:     if (b.key_id != null) {
789:       const kk = `${key}:${b.key_id}`;
790:       let ka = keyAcc.get(kk);
791:       if (!ka) keyAcc.set(kk, ka = emptyAcc());
792:       addBucket(ka, w, b);
793:     }
794:   }
795: 
796:   // Calendar-month token usage per model, for the headroom guardrail.
797:   const usageRows = db.prepare(`
798:     SELECT platform, model_id, key_id, COALESCE(SUM(input_tokens + output_tokens), 0) AS used
799:     FROM requests
800:     WHERE created_at >= datetime('now', 'start of month')
801:       AND request_type = 'chat'
802:     GROUP BY platform, model_id, key_id
803:   `).all() as Array<{ platform: string; model_id: string; key_id: number | null; used: number }>;
804:   const usageMap = new Map<string, number>();
805:   for (const r of usageRows) {
806:     const key = modelStatsKey(r.platform, r.model_id, scopeOf(r.platform, r.key_id));
807:     usageMap.set(key, (usageMap.get(key) ?? 0) + r.used);
808:   }
809: 
810:   const next = new Map<string, ModelStats>();
811:   for (const [key, a] of acc) {
812:     next.set(key, {
813:       successes: a.wSucc,
814:       failures: a.wFail,
815:       tokPerSec: a.wLat > 0 ? (a.wOut * 1000) / a.wLat : 0,
816:       avgTtfbMs: a.wTtfbCnt > 0 ? a.wTtfbSum / a.wTtfbCnt : null,
817:       monthlyUsedTokens: usageMap.get(key) ?? 0,
818:       speedSamples: a.wSucc + a.wTimeouts,
819:     });
820:   }
821:   // Models with month usage but no recent window data still need a headroom number.
822:   for (const [key, used] of usageMap) {
823:     if (!next.has(key)) {
824:       next.set(key, { successes: 0, failures: 0, tokPerSec: 0, avgTtfbMs: null, monthlyUsedTokens: used, speedSamples: 0 });
825:     }
826:   }
827: 
828:   const nextKeys = new Map<string, KeyStats>();
829:   for (const [kk, a] of keyAcc) {
830:     nextKeys.set(kk, {
831:       successes: a.wSucc,
832:       failures: a.wFail,
833:       tokPerSec: a.wLat > 0 ? (a.wOut * 1000) / a.wLat : 0,
834:       avgTtfbMs: a.wTtfbCnt > 0 ? a.wTtfbSum / a.wTtfbCnt : null,
835:     });
836:   }
837: 
838:   statsCache = next;
839:   keyStatsCache = nextKeys;
840:   statsCacheTime = Date.now();
841: 
842:   // Natural tail of a recompute: fold what we just measured back into
843:   // models.speed_rank (#619). Never allowed to break routing — the caches above
844:   // are already published, and a failed write just means the column keeps its
845:   // previous value until the next pass.
846:   if (Date.now() - speedRankWriteTime >= SPEED_RANK_WRITE_INTERVAL_MS) {
847:     speedRankWriteTime = Date.now();
848:     try {
849:       writeObservedSpeedRanks(db);
850:     } catch (e) {
851:       console.error('Failed to write observed speed ranks:', e);
852:     }
853:   }
854: }
855: 
856: // ── Observed speed_rank writeback (#619) ────────────────────────────────────
857: // models.speed_rank is the catalog's hand-assigned speed ordering and drives
858: // the dashboard's sort-by-speed preset. It was only ever WRITTEN by the seed
859: // migrations, catalog sync, and an explicit user override — never by anything
860: // that had actually watched the model run, so a relay model that hangs on half
861: // its calls kept whatever rank the catalog guessed for it forever.
862: //
863: // This folds the live speed axis back into the column, under three rules:
864: //   - a model needs SPEED_RANK_MIN_SAMPLES decay-weighted speed-bearing
865: //     requests (successes + timeouts) before we claim to know anything; below
866: //     that it keeps its catalog value;
867: //   - a user-set speed_rank override always wins — we skip those models
868: //     entirely rather than fight applyModelOverrides for the column;
869: //   - the UPDATE is guarded on the value actually changing, so a steady system
870: //     writes nothing at all.
871: //
872: // A catalog sync re-stamps speed_rank from the catalog; the next pass simply
873: // re-derives the observed value, which is why this is a periodic write rather
874: // than a one-shot migration.
875: export const SPEED_RANK_MIN_SAMPLES = 20;
876: const SPEED_RANK_WRITE_INTERVAL_MS = 10 * 60 * 1000;
877: let speedRankWriteTime = 0;
878: 
879: /** Test hook: forget when the last writeback ran so the next refresh does one. */
880: export function resetSpeedRankWriteback(): void {
881:   speedRankWriteTime = 0;
882: }
883: 
884: /**
885:  * Write an observed speed rank for every model with enough recent samples and
886:  * no user-set speed_rank override. Returns how many rows actually changed.
887:  * Reads the stats cache as-is — callers refresh it first (refreshStatsCache
888:  * calls this from its own tail).
889:  */
890: export function writeObservedSpeedRanks(db: Db): number {
891:   if (!statsCache || statsCache.size === 0) return 0;
892: 
893:   const pinned = modelsWithOverriddenField(db, 'speedRank');
894:   const rows = db.prepare('SELECT id, platform, model_id, speed_rank, endpoint_scope FROM models')
895:     .all() as { id: number; platform: string; model_id: string; speed_rank: number; endpoint_scope: string }[];
896: 
897:   const update = db.prepare('UPDATE models SET speed_rank = ? WHERE id = ?');
898:   let written = 0;
899:   const tx = db.transaction(() => {
900:     for (const row of rows) {
901:       // Overrides are keyed (platform, model_id) — they only exist for
902:       // catalog-managed rows, which are never endpoint-scoped — while the
903:       // measured stats are per endpoint, so each relay's copy gets its own
904:       // observed rank instead of one shared number (#651).
905:       if (pinned.has(`${row.platform}:${row.model_id}`)) continue;
906:       const stats = statsCache!.get(modelStatsKey(row.platform, row.model_id, row.endpoint_scope));
907:       if (!stats || stats.speedSamples < SPEED_RANK_MIN_SAMPLES) continue;
908:       const rank = observedSpeedRank(speedScore(stats.tokPerSec, stats.avgTtfbMs));
909:       if (rank === row.speed_rank) continue;
910:       update.run(rank, row.id);
911:       written++;
912:     }
913:   });
914:   tx();
915:   return written;
916: }
917: 
918: // Composite intelligence (tier-first, rank-as-tiebreaker) lives in scoring.ts
919: // so the seeding path can reason about the same tier ladder the router scores
920: // on — see intelligenceComposite there.
921: 
922: // Per-model axis values + the final score. `sampled` chooses Thompson sampling
923: // (for routing) vs. the expected value (for a stable dashboard display).
924: interface ScoredEntry {
925:   axes: { reliability: number; speed: number; intelligence: number };
926:   headroom: number;
927:   rateLimit: number;
928:   score: number;
929: }
930: 
931: // Enabled + healthy/unknown key count per platform, for pooled-budget scaling.
932: // This is the SAME filter both /api/fallback endpoints use (issue #456): the
933: // monthly budget is a PER-KEY free-tier allowance, so N usable keys pool N× the
934: // capacity. `monthlyUsedTokens` is already summed across all keys, so budget
935: // must scale to match or the headroom guardrail damps a multi-key model to the
936: // floor after just one account's worth of tokens.
937: function usableKeyCountsByPlatform(db: Db): Map<string, number> {
938:   const rows = db.prepare(
939:     "SELECT platform, COUNT(*) AS count FROM api_keys WHERE enabled = 1 AND status IN ('healthy', 'unknown') GROUP BY platform"
940:   ).all() as { platform: string; count: number }[];
941:   return new Map(rows.map(r => [r.platform, r.count]));
942: }
943: 
944: function scoreChainEntry(
945:   entry: ChainRow,
946:   weights: RoutingWeights,
947:   intelMin: number,
948:   intelMax: number,
949:   sampled: boolean,
950:   keyCounts: Map<string, number>,
951:   headroomCfg: HeadroomThresholds,
952: ): ScoredEntry {
953:   const stats = statsCache?.get(modelStatsKey(entry.platform, entry.model_id, entry.endpoint_scope));
954:   const successes = stats?.successes ?? 0;
955:   const failures = stats?.failures ?? 0;
956: 
957:   const community = activeCommunityPrior(entry.platform, entry.model_id, entry.endpoint_scope);
958:   let reliability: number;
959:   if (sampled) {
960:     const { alpha, beta } = reliabilityPosterior(successes, failures, community);
961:     reliability = sampleBeta(alpha, beta);
962:   } else {
963:     reliability = expectedReliability(successes, failures, community);
964:   }
965: 
966:   const speed = speedScore(stats?.tokPerSec ?? 0, stats?.avgTtfbMs ?? null);
967:   const intelligence = intelligenceScore(
968:     intelligenceComposite(entry.size_label, entry.intelligence_rank), intelMin, intelMax,
969:   );
970: 
971:   // Scale the per-key monthly budget by the usable key count for this platform,
972:   // matching the pooled `monthlyUsedTokens` aggregate (#456). Math.max(1, …) so a
973:   // model whose platform currently has no usable key isn't handed a 0 budget.
974:   const budget = parseBudget(entry.monthly_token_budget) * Math.max(1, keyCounts.get(entry.platform) ?? 1);
975:   // Tunable headroom thresholds (#899): persisted overrides for when demotion
976:   // starts and its floor; absent settings keep the scoring.ts defaults. Read
977:   // ONCE per chain by the caller, not per entry — getSetting is an uncached
978:   // SELECT, so reading it here cost two extra SQLite round-trips per model per
979:   // request, the same reason `weights` and `keyCounts` are hoisted.
980:   const monthlyHeadroom = headroomFactor(stats?.monthlyUsedTokens ?? 0, budget, headroomCfg);
981: 
982:   // The same guardrail, driven by live rpm/rpd/tpm/tpd utilization instead of
983:   // the monthly budget (#899). Most free tiers publish a daily request or token
984:   // cap and no monthly figure at all, so without this a model sits at score #1
985:   // until the request that finally 429s it. Reads a snapshot memoised inside
986:   // ratelimit.ts, so this costs no query per model per request.
987:   const windowHeadroom = rateWindowHeadroomFactor(
988:     modelWindowUsedFraction(
989:       { platform: entry.platform, modelId: entry.model_id, keyId: entry.key_id },
990:       { rpm: entry.rpm_limit, rpd: entry.rpd_limit, tpm: entry.tpm_limit, tpd: entry.tpd_limit },
991:     ),
992:     headroomCfg,
993:   );
994: 
995:   // The WORSE of the two, not their product: both express the same "this model
996:   // is close to burning out" opinion on different meters, and multiplying them
997:   // would push a model that is low on both to floor², below the floor the
998:   // operator configured. Taking the binding constraint keeps the floor meaning
999:   // what it says — the same rule getKeyQuotaHeadroom applies across metrics.
1000:   const headroom = Math.min(monthlyHeadroom, windowHeadroom);
1001:   const rl = rateLimitFactor(getPenalty(entry.model_db_id));
1002: 
1003:   // Per-model env overrides (#738) scale the final score so a slow or
1004:   // poor-quality model is demoted without being disabled outright — a manual
1005:   // 'priority' chain can still select it.
1006:   const score = applyModelWeightOverride(
1007:     combineScore({ reliability, speed, intelligence, headroom, rateLimit: rl }, weights),
1008:     entry.model_id,
1009:   );
1010:   return { axes: { reliability, speed, intelligence }, headroom, rateLimit: rl, score };
1011: }
1012: 
1013: /**
1014:  * Order the enabled fallback chain for routing.
1015:  *  - 'priority' strategy → legacy manual order + 429 penalty (unchanged).
1016:  *  - bandit strategy      → convex score, manual priority as the deterministic
1017:  *                           tiebreaker for (near-)equal scores.
1018:  *
1019:  * `sampled` controls the bandit branch: Thompson sampling (the default) for
1020:  * live routing, where per-call randomness is the exploration the bandit needs;
1021:  * the deterministic expected score (`sampled = false`) for callers that want a
1022:  * STABLE ranking under the chosen strategy — the fusion panel, which should be a
1023:  * faithful reflection of the user's picked strategy, not a re-sampled draw each
1024:  * request. Priority mode is deterministic either way.
1025:  */
1026: function orderChain(chain: ChainRow[], strategy: RoutingStrategy, sampled = true): ChainRow[] {
1027:   // Tier first, always: it is the one ordering input that score must not be able
1028:   // to override (see ChainRow.match_tier). Zero for every chain built anywhere
1029:   // else, so this is a no-op outside slug-fallback resolution.
1030:   const tier = (e: ChainRow) => e.match_tier ?? 0;
1031:   const weights = weightsFor(strategy);
1032:   if (!weights) {
1033:     // Legacy priority mode: manual chain order + the 429/failure penalty,
1034:     // ascending.

1118:  * the entire catalog instead, while the same chain addressed by name
1119:  * (`auto:<name>`) correctly refused. `fallback_config` is the chain only for an
1120:  * install with no profile at all.
1121:  */
1122: function getActiveChain(db: Db): ChainRow[] {
1123:   const profileId = getActiveProfileId(db);
1124:   if (profileId != null) {
1125:     return db.prepare(`
1126:       SELECT pm.model_db_id, pm.priority, pm.enabled,
1127:              m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name, m.intelligence_rank,
1128:              m.size_label, m.monthly_token_budget,
1129:              m.rpm_limit, m.rpd_limit, m.tpm_limit, m.tpd_limit, m.supports_vision,
1130:              m.supports_tools, m.context_window, m.key_id, m.endpoint_scope
1131:       FROM profile_models pm
1132:       JOIN models m ON m.id = pm.model_db_id AND m.enabled = 1
1133:       WHERE pm.profile_id = ?
1134:       ORDER BY pm.priority ASC
1135:     `).all(profileId) as ChainRow[];
1136:   }
1137: 
1138:   return db.prepare(`
1139:     SELECT fc.model_db_id, fc.priority, fc.enabled,
1140:            m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name, m.intelligence_rank,
1141:            m.size_label, m.monthly_token_budget,
1142:            m.rpm_limit, m.rpd_limit, m.tpm_limit, m.tpd_limit, m.supports_vision,
1143:            m.supports_tools, m.context_window, m.key_id, m.endpoint_scope
1144:     FROM fallback_config fc
1145:     JOIN models m ON m.id = fc.model_db_id AND m.enabled = 1
1146:     ORDER BY fc.priority ASC
1147:   `).all() as ChainRow[];
1148: }

1150: function getChainByProfileName(db: Db, name: string): ChainRow[] | null {
1151:   const profile = db.prepare("SELECT id FROM profiles WHERE LOWER(name) = ?").get(name.toLowerCase()) as { id: number } | undefined;
1152:   if (!profile) return null;
1153: 
1154:   return db.prepare(`
1155:     SELECT pm.model_db_id, pm.priority, pm.enabled,
1156:            m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name, m.intelligence_rank,
1157:            m.size_label, m.monthly_token_budget,
1158:            m.rpm_limit, m.rpd_limit, m.tpm_limit, m.tpd_limit, m.supports_vision,
1159:            m.supports_tools, m.context_window, m.key_id, m.endpoint_scope
1160:     FROM profile_models pm
1161:     JOIN models m ON m.id = pm.model_db_id AND m.enabled = 1
1162:     WHERE pm.profile_id = ?
1163:     ORDER BY pm.priority ASC
1164:   `).all(profile.id) as ChainRow[];

1167: function getChainByGlobalSort(db: Db, globalAxis: string): ChainRow[] {
1168:   // A global sort ignores the chain's ORDER, not its enable flags: a model the
1169:   // operator switched off — in the catalog or just for auto routing — stays off
1170:   // here too (#634). Models with no chain row yet (fresh catalog rows) default
1171:   // to in, so the sort still spans the whole catalog.
1172:   const profileId = getActiveProfileId(db);
1173:   const chainEnabled = profileId != null
1174:     ? 'COALESCE(pm.enabled, fc.enabled, 1) = 1'
1175:     : 'COALESCE(fc.enabled, 1) = 1';
1176:   const allEnabled = db.prepare(`
1177:     SELECT m.id as model_db_id, 0 as priority, 1 as enabled,
1178:            m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name, m.intelligence_rank,
1179:            m.size_label, m.monthly_token_budget,
1180:            m.rpm_limit, m.rpd_limit, m.tpm_limit, m.tpd_limit, m.supports_vision,
1181:            m.supports_tools, m.context_window, m.key_id, m.endpoint_scope
1182:     FROM models m
1183:     LEFT JOIN fallback_config fc ON fc.model_db_id = m.id
1184:     ${profileId != null ? 'LEFT JOIN profile_models pm ON pm.profile_id = ? AND pm.model_db_id = m.id' : ''}
1185:     WHERE m.enabled = 1 AND ${chainEnabled}
1186:   `).all(...(profileId != null ? [profileId] : [])) as ChainRow[];
1187: 
1188:   const strategyMap: Record<string, RoutingStrategy> = {
1189:     'smart': 'smartest',
1190:     'fast': 'fastest',
1191:     'cheap': 'balanced',
1192:     'reliable': 'reliable',
1193:     'balanced': 'balanced'
1194:   };
1195:   const strat = strategyMap[globalAxis] || 'balanced';
1196:   
1197:   return orderChain(allEnabled, strat);
1198: }

1200: /**
1201:  * The active chain, or a client-facing refusal when it has nothing enabled.
1202:  *
1203:  * Mirrors what `auto:<name>` already does for a named chain: say the chain is
1204:  * empty rather than routing the request over models the operator never put in
1205:  * it. Only when a profile is active — a legacy install with none keeps the
1206:  * ordinary "all models exhausted" exhaustion path.
1207:  */
1208: function activeChainOrThrow(db: Db): ChainRow[] {
1209:   const chain = getActiveChain(db);
1210:   if (chain.some(entry => entry.enabled)) return chain;
1211: 
1212:   const profileId = getActiveProfileId(db);
1213:   if (profileId == null) return chain;
1214: 
1215:   const profile = db.prepare('SELECT name FROM profiles WHERE id = ?').get(profileId) as { name: string } | undefined;
1216:   const err = new Error(
1217:     `The active fallback chain${profile ? ` '${profile.name}'` : ''} has no enabled models. `
1218:     + 'Enable models for it on the Models page, switch the active chain, or name another one with "auto:<chain>".',
1219:   ) as any;
1220:   err.status = 400;
1221:   throw err;
1222: }

1224: export function resolveRoutingChain(modelString: string | undefined): ResolvedChain {
1225:   const db = getDb();
1226: 
1227:   if (!modelString || modelString.toLowerCase() === 'auto') {
1228:     return { chain: activeChainOrThrow(db), strategyKey: 'auto' };
1229:   }
1230: 
1231:   const lower = modelString.toLowerCase();
1232:   if (!lower.startsWith('auto:')) {
1233:     return { chain: activeChainOrThrow(db), strategyKey: 'auto' };
1234:   }
1235: 
1236:   const suffix = lower.slice('auto:'.length).trim();
1237:   if (!suffix) {
1238:     return { chain: activeChainOrThrow(db), strategyKey: 'auto' };
1239:   }
1240: 
1241:   const globalAxis = GLOBAL_SORT_ALIASES[suffix];
1242:   if (globalAxis) {
1243:     const chain = getChainByGlobalSort(db, globalAxis);
1244:     if (chain.length === 0) {
1245:       const err = new Error(`No enabled models available for global sort '${suffix}'`) as any;
1246:       err.status = 400;
1247:       throw err;
1248:     }
1249:     return { chain, strategyKey: `auto:${globalAxis}` };
1250:   }
1251: 
1252:   const chain = getChainByProfileName(db, suffix);
1253:   if (!chain) {
1254:     const err = new Error(`Profile '${suffix}' not found. Use 'auto' for the default profile, or call /v1/models for available options.`) as any;
1255:     err.status = 400;
1256:     throw err;
1257:   }
1258: 
1259:   const enabledModels = chain.filter(e => e.enabled);
1260:   if (enabledModels.length === 0) {
1261:     const err = new Error(`Profile '${suffix}' has no enabled models. Add models to this profile in the dashboard.`) as any;
1262:     err.status = 400;
1263:     throw err;
1264:   }
1265: 
1266:   return { chain, strategyKey: `auto:${suffix}` };
1267: }

1269: // Weights for the in-model key score (#580). Reliability dominates: the point
1270: // of per-key stats is catching a credential that FAILS (expired, drained,
1271: // region-blocked); speed differences between keys of the same platform+model
1272: // are second-order (account-tier throttling) but still worth a nudge.
1273: const KEY_SCORE_WEIGHTS = { reliability: 0.75, speed: 0.25 };
1274: 
1275: /**
1276:  * Order a model's candidate keys by a Thompson-sampled per-key score, mirroring
1277:  * orderChain's bandit: reliability is a fresh draw from each key's Beta
1278:  * posterior (so exploration is automatic and proportional to uncertainty — a
1279:  * key with no data samples from the uniform prior and still gets traffic),
1280:  * speed is deterministic. Returns null when NO key has recorded data, telling
1281:  * the caller to keep the legacy round-robin rotation (no signal → no ranking).
1282:  */
1283: function orderKeysByScore(entry: ChainRow, keys: KeyRow[]): KeyRow[] | null {
1284:   if (keys.length < 2 || !keyStatsCache) return null;
1285:   const prefix = `${modelStatsKey(entry.platform, entry.model_id, entry.endpoint_scope)}:`;
1286:   if (!keys.some(k => keyStatsCache!.has(prefix + k.id))) return null;
1287: 
1288:   // The prior is per-model, not per-key: look it up once outside the loop.
1289:   const community = activeCommunityPrior(entry.platform, entry.model_id, entry.endpoint_scope);
1290:   return keys
1291:     .map(k => {
1292:       const stats = keyStatsCache!.get(prefix + k.id);
1293:       const { alpha, beta } = reliabilityPosterior(stats?.successes ?? 0, stats?.failures ?? 0, community);
1294:       const rel = sampleBeta(alpha, beta);
1295:       const spd = speedScore(stats?.tokPerSec ?? 0, stats?.avgTtfbMs ?? null);
1296:       return { k, s: KEY_SCORE_WEIGHTS.reliability * rel + KEY_SCORE_WEIGHTS.speed * spd };
1297:     })
1298:     .sort((a, b) => b.s - a.s || a.k.id - b.k.id)
1299:     .map(x => x.k);
1300: }
1301: 
1302: /** Headroom assumed for a key the quota tracker has never seen. Neutral on
1303:  *  purpose: an unobserved budget is no reason to prefer a key (it could be
1304:  *  drained) and no reason to avoid one (it could be untouched), so it sorts
1305:  *  between an exhausted key and a fresh one and otherwise keeps its incoming
1306:  *  round-robin position. */
1307: const UNKNOWN_QUOTA_HEADROOM = 0.5;
1308: 
1309: /**
1310:  * Whether remaining-quota weighting is meaningful for this chain entry: the
1311:  * operator asked for it AND the platform meters its keys separately.
1312:  *
1313:  * An account-scoped pool ('<platform>::account') is ONE budget every key of the
1314:  * account draws down, so "which key has more left" has no answer — every key
1315:  * reports the same number, and reordering on it would only churn the rotation
1316:  * for nothing (#919).
1317:  */
1318: function quotaWeightingApplies(entry: ChainRow): boolean {
1319:   if (getKeySelectionStrategy() !== 'least-remaining') return false;
1320:   return !inferQuotaPoolKey(entry.platform as Platform, entry.model_id).endsWith('::account');
1321: }
1322: 
1323: /**
1324:  * Re-order an already-ordered candidate list by observed remaining quota,
1325:  * roomiest first (#919 — the issue asks for higher-remaining-first, so the key
1326:  * nearest its cap is tried last, not first).
1327:  *
1328:  * Deliberately a SORT over the caller's list rather than a second walk: the
1329:  * incoming order is the round-robin rotation (or the per-key bandit ranking),
1330:  * and Array#sort is stable, so keys with equal headroom — including the common
1331:  * case of no observations at all — keep exactly the order they would have had.
1332:  * Every gate, the custom-endpoint filter and the skip tally stay in the one
1333:  * walk that follows.
1334:  */
1335: function orderKeysByRemainingQuota(entry: ChainRow, ordered: KeyRow[]): KeyRow[] {
1336:   const headroom = getKeyQuotaHeadroom(entry.platform as Platform);
1337:   if (headroom.size === 0) return ordered;
1338:   // Hoisted out of the comparator: sort calls it O(n log n) times, and the
1339:   // lookup below must not re-derive anything per comparison.
1340:   const room = new Map(ordered.map(k => [k.id, headroom.get(k.id) ?? UNKNOWN_QUOTA_HEADROOM]));
1341:   return [...ordered].sort((a, b) => room.get(b.id)! - room.get(a.id)!);
1342: }
1343: 
1344: /**
1345:  * Pick a usable key for ONE model and build its RouteResult, or return null if
1346:  * the model has no key that can serve the request right now (all cooled down,
1347:  * over quota, undecryptable, or no provider). Factored out of routeRequest so
1348:  * the fusion panel can HARD-PIN a model: walk that model's keys without ever
1349:  * falling through to a different model (issue #326 — soft preference collapses
1350:  * panel diversity under rate limits). Keys are tried in per-key bandit-score
1351:  * order when any of them has recorded data (#580), else round-robin.
1352:  * Request-level filters (vision/tools/context window) stay in the caller; this
1353:  * only does key selection + accounting pre-checks.
1354:  */
1355: function selectKeyForModel(entry: ChainRow, estimatedTokens: number, skipKeys?: Set<string>, diag?: string[]): RouteResult | null {
1356:   const db = getDb();
1357:   const label = `${entry.platform}/${entry.model_id}`;
1358: 
1359:   if (!hasProvider(entry.platform as Platform)) {
1360:     diag?.push(`${label}: no provider registered`);
1361:     return null;
1362:   }
1363:   const provider = getProvider(entry.platform as Platform)!;
1364: 
1365:   const allKeys = db.prepare(
1366:     "SELECT * FROM api_keys WHERE platform = ? AND enabled = 1 AND status IN ('healthy', 'unknown')"
1367:   ).all(entry.platform) as KeyRow[];
1368:   if (allKeys.length === 0) {
1369:     diag?.push(`${label}: no enabled+healthy key for platform`);
1370:     return null;
1371:   }
1372: 
1373:   // Scoped keys (#657) are dropped before the walk: a key whose model scope
1374:   // excludes this model is not a candidate at all — it neither takes a
1375:   // round-robin slot nor burns an attempt on a guaranteed 403. Parsed once per
1376:   // key row.
1377:   const keys = allKeys.filter(k => scopeAllows(parseModelScope(k.model_scope_json), entry.model_id));
1378:   if (keys.length === 0) {
1379:     diag?.push(`${label}: no usable key — ${allKeys.length} key(s) scoped to other models`);
1380:     return null;
1381:   }
1382: 
1383:   // Tally the gate that rejected each key, so the exhaustion diagnostic can say
1384:   // *why* a model with keys still couldn't serve (all on cooldown vs over quota).
1385:   const skipTally: Record<string, number> = {};
1386:   const note = (reason: string) => { skipTally[reason] = (skipTally[reason] ?? 0) + 1; };
1387: 
1388:   const limits = {
1389:     rpm: entry.rpm_limit,
1390:     rpd: entry.rpd_limit,
1391:     tpm: entry.tpm_limit,
1392:     tpd: entry.tpd_limit,
1393:   };
1394: 
1395:   // Score-ordered walk over this model's keys (#580): when any key has recorded
1396:   // reliability/speed data, try them best-sampled-score first so a chronically
1397:   // failing key stops soaking up every Nth request. The stats cache is the same
1398:   // 60s-TTL aggregate the model-level bandit uses (refresh is a no-op when
1399:   // fresh, and cheap when not). With no data at all, keep the legacy rotation.
1400:   refreshStatsCache(db);
1401:   // Scoped so two relays offering the same model id don't share one rotation
1402:   // cursor over the platform's key list (#651).
1403:   const rrKey = modelStatsKey(entry.platform, entry.model_id, entry.endpoint_scope);
1404:   let idx = roundRobinIndex.get(rrKey) ?? 0;
1405:   let ranked = orderKeysByScore(entry, keys);
1406: 
1407:   // Remaining-quota weighting (#919) layers on top: it re-sorts whatever order
1408:   // we were going to walk anyway — the bandit ranking when there is per-key
1409:   // data, otherwise the round-robin rotation starting at the live cursor — so
1410:   // ties fall back to that order instead of to rowid.
1411:   if (keys.length > 1 && quotaWeightingApplies(entry)) {
1412:     const base = ranked ?? Array.from({ length: keys.length }, (_, i) => keys[(idx + i) % keys.length]);
1413:     ranked = orderKeysByRemainingQuota(entry, base);
1414:   }
1415: 
1416:   // A custom model belongs to exactly one endpoint (#212), but an endpoint can
1417:    // hold several credentials — so the pool is every key on the same base_url,
1418:    // rotated like any other platform's keys (#619). Legacy rows (key_id NULL)
1419:    // keep the old any-key match.
1420:    const endpointKeyIds = entry.platform === 'custom' && entry.key_id != null
1421:      ? customEndpointKeyIds(db, entry.key_id)
1422:      : null;
1423: 
1424: 
1425:   for (let attempt = 0; attempt < keys.length; attempt++) {
1426:     const key = ranked ? ranked[attempt] : keys[(idx + attempt) % keys.length];
1427:     const skipId = `${entry.platform}:${entry.model_id}:${key.id}`;
1428:     
1429:     // Skip if this key was already tried and failed in this request
1430:     if (skipKeys?.has(skipId)) { note('already-failed-this-request'); continue; }
1431: 
1432:     // For custom models, ensure the key belongs to the correct endpoint
1433:     if (endpointKeyIds && !endpointKeyIds.has(key.id)) { note('custom-key-mismatch'); continue; }
1434: 
1435:     if (isOnCooldown(entry.platform, entry.model_id, key.id)) { note('cooldown'); continue; }
1436:     if (!canUseProvider(entry.platform, key.id)) { note('provider-daily-cap'); continue; }
1437:     // Account-wide per-minute budget, checked before the per-model gates: a model
1438:     // with a NULL rpm_limit would otherwise sail past them and spend a budget its
1439:     // siblings share.
1440:     if (!canUseProviderMinute(entry.platform, key.id)) { note('provider-minute-cap'); continue; }
1441:     // Skip a key that already has its allowed requests in the air. Without this,
1442:     // parallel streams all pick the same key and 429 each other on providers that
1443:     // meter concurrency per credential.
1444:     if (!canUseKeyConcurrency(entry.platform, key.id)) { note('key-concurrency'); continue; }
1445:     if (!canMakeRequest(entry.platform, entry.model_id, key.id, limits)) { note('rpm/rpd-limit'); continue; }
1446:     if (!canUseTokens(entry.platform, entry.model_id, key.id, estimatedTokens, limits)) { note('tpm/tpd-limit'); continue; }
1447:     if (!canUseProviderTokens(entry.platform, key.id, entry.model_id, estimatedTokens)) { note('provider-daily-token-cap'); continue; }
1448: 
1449:     let decryptedKey: string;
1450:     try {
1451:       decryptedKey = decrypt(key.encrypted_key, key.iv, key.auth_tag);
1452:     } catch {
1453:       db.prepare("UPDATE api_keys SET status = 'error', last_checked_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ?")
1454:         .run(key.id);
1455:       note('decrypt-error');
1456:       continue;
1457:     }
1458: 
1459:     const resolvedProvider = entry.platform === 'custom'
1460:       ? resolveProvider('custom', key.base_url)
1461:       : provider;
1462:     if (!resolvedProvider) { note('no-resolved-provider'); continue; }
1463: 
1464:     roundRobinIndex.set(rrKey, idx);
1465:     // Taken only once the key has cleared every gate and is definitely being
1466:     // returned, so a rejected candidate never consumes concurrency budget.
1467:     const leaseId = acquireLease(entry.platform, entry.model_id, key.id, estimatedTokens);
1468:     return {
1469:       provider: resolvedProvider,
1470:       modelId: entry.model_id,
1471:       modelDbId: entry.model_db_id,
1472:       apiKey: decryptedKey,
1473:       keyId: key.id,
1474:       keyLabel: key.label || null,
1475:       // Decrypted once here, at the point the row is already in hand (#590).
1476:       proxyUrl: decryptProxyUrl(key),
1477:       platform: entry.platform,
1478:       displayName: entry.display_name,
1479:       endpointScope: entry.endpoint_scope ?? '',
1480:       rpdLimit: limits.rpd,
1481:       tpdLimit: limits.tpd,
1482:       release: () => releaseLease(leaseId),
1483:     };
1484:   }
1485: 
1486:   // No usable key for this model. Advance the round-robin index anyway so we
1487:   // don't get stuck re-trying the same exhausted key first next time.
1488:   roundRobinIndex.set(rrKey, idx);
1489:   const summary = Object.entries(skipTally).map(([r, n]) => `${r}:${n}`).join(', ') || 'no usable key';
1490:   diag?.push(`${label}: ${keys.length} key(s) — ${summary}`);
1491:   return null;
1492: }
1493: 
1494: /**
1495:  * Whether the model still has ANOTHER key that could serve it right now, given
1496:  * the key that just failed (excludingKeyId) and any keys already ruled out this
1497:  * request (skipKeys, in the "platform:modelId:keyId" form). Applies the same
1498:  * gates selectKeyForModel uses — enabled + healthy status, not on cooldown,
1499:  * under the provider daily cap, and under rpm/rpd/tpm/tpd — so the answer means
1500:  * "a real, dispatchable alternative exists".
1501:  *
1502:  * Used by the retry loops to decide whether a single key's 429 should demote the
1503:  * WHOLE model (the model-level 429 penalty). It should not: the per-key cooldown
1504:  * already isolates the failing key, so demoting the model while a sibling key can
1505:  * still serve it wrongly sinks a healthy model in the scorer (#454). We only
1506:  * record the model-level hit when this returns false — i.e. the 429 exhausted the
1507:  * model, not just one of its keys.
1508:  */
1509: export function hasOtherUsableKey(modelDbId: number, excludingKeyId: number, skipKeys?: Set<string>): boolean {
1510:   const db = getDb();
1511:   const m = db.prepare(`
1512:     SELECT platform, model_id, rpm_limit, rpd_limit, tpm_limit, tpd_limit, key_id
1513:       FROM models WHERE id = ?
1514:   `).get(modelDbId) as {
1515:     platform: string; model_id: string;
1516:     rpm_limit: number | null; rpd_limit: number | null;
1517:     tpm_limit: number | null; tpd_limit: number | null; key_id: number | null;
1518:   } | undefined;
1519:   if (!m) return false;
1520: 
1521:   const limits = { rpm: m.rpm_limit, rpd: m.rpd_limit, tpm: m.tpm_limit, tpd: m.tpd_limit };
1522:   const keys = db.prepare(
1523:     "SELECT id, model_scope_json FROM api_keys WHERE platform = ? AND enabled = 1 AND status IN ('healthy', 'unknown')"
1524:   ).all(m.platform) as { id: number; model_scope_json: string | null }[];
1525: 
1526:   // Keys of the model's own custom endpoint (#212, #619); a key belonging to a
1527:   // DIFFERENT endpoint cannot serve it, so it doesn't count as an alternative.
1528:   const endpointKeyIds = m.platform === 'custom' && m.key_id != null
1529:     ? customEndpointKeyIds(db, m.key_id)
1530:     : null;
1531: 
1532:   for (const k of keys) {
1533:     if (k.id === excludingKeyId) continue;
1534:     if (endpointKeyIds && !endpointKeyIds.has(k.id)) continue;
1535:     // A sibling scoped away from this model can never serve it (#657) — counting
1536:     // it would wrongly suppress the model-level penalty this gate exists for.
1537:     if (!scopeAllows(parseModelScope(k.model_scope_json), m.model_id)) continue;
1538:     if (skipKeys?.has(`${m.platform}:${m.model_id}:${k.id}`)) continue;
1539:     if (isOnCooldown(m.platform, m.model_id, k.id)) continue;
1540:     if (!canUseProvider(m.platform, k.id)) continue;
1541:     if (!canUseProviderMinute(m.platform, k.id)) continue;
1542:     if (!canMakeRequest(m.platform, m.model_id, k.id, limits)) continue;
1543:     // A per-minute token spike on the failed key doesn't mean a fresh key lacks
1544:     // headroom; a nominal 1-token probe only rules out a key already at its
1545:     // TPM/TPD ceiling.
1546:     if (!canUseTokens(m.platform, m.model_id, k.id, 1, limits)) continue;
1547:     if (!canUseProviderTokens(m.platform, k.id, m.model_id, 1)) continue;
1548:     return true;
1549:   }
1550:   return false;
1551: }
1552: 
1553: /**
1554:  * Every key that can be ROUTED to this model: enabled + healthy/unknown, not

1584: function getModelChainRow(db: Db, modelDbId: number): ChainRow | undefined {
1585:   return db.prepare(`
1586:     SELECT m.id as model_db_id, 0 as priority, 1 as enabled,
1587:            m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name, m.intelligence_rank,
1588:            m.size_label, m.monthly_token_budget,
1589:            m.rpm_limit, m.rpd_limit, m.tpm_limit, m.tpd_limit, m.supports_vision,
1590:            m.supports_tools, m.context_window, m.key_id, m.endpoint_scope
1591:     FROM models m
1592:     WHERE m.id = ? AND m.enabled = 1
1593:   `).get(modelDbId) as ChainRow | undefined;
1594: }

1596: /**
1597:  * Safety margin applied when ranking a model against an estimated request size.
1598:  * The estimate is a chars/4 heuristic that under-counts dense payloads (JSON,
1599:  * code, CJK) by up to ~2x; without any accounting for that gap such requests
1600:  * were routed to models whose real tokenizer count exceeded the window and the
1601:  * provider rejected them with a 400 mid-chain (kilo: "maximum context length is
1602:  * 262144 tokens" on requests estimated <=256000).
1603:  *
1604:  * The margin is a SOFT preference, not a hard filter (#956 review): /v1/models
1605:  * advertises the RAW window, so clients legitimately pack requests right up to
1606:  * it. Excluding margin-violating models outright would turn an upstream 400
1607:  * that the retry loop already classifies and handles (`context_too_large`)
1608:  * into a regression: "all models exhausted" with zero attempts. Callers
1609:  * therefore try margin-fitting candidates first and only fall back to raw
1610:  * advertised-window fits (see fitsContextWindowStrict) when nothing else can
1611:  * serve the request.
1612:  */
1613: export const CONTEXT_WINDOW_SAFETY_FACTOR = 1.25;
1614: 
1615: // Platforms whose pre-dispatch trim guard already caps the dispatched input
1616: // below the live context ceiling (lib/content.ts truncateMessagesForGithub):
1617: // the guard — not the routing estimate — is what guarantees the fit there, so
1618: // applying the factor too would only make that guard unreachable. The margin
1619: // checks below treat these platforms as strict comparisons.
1620: const TRIM_GUARDED_PLATFORMS = new Set(['github']);
1621: 
1622: /** True when `estimatedTokens` fits the RAW advertised window (null window =
1623:  * unknown, never filtered — same convention as the auto-router). This is the
1624:  * comparison /v1/models publishes and the soft-preference fallback tier. */
1625: export function fitsContextWindowStrict(contextWindow: number | null | undefined, estimatedTokens: number): boolean {
1626:   return contextWindow == null || estimatedTokens <= contextWindow;
1627: }
1628: 
1629: /** True when `estimatedTokens` plausibly fits `contextWindow` WITH the safety
1630:  * margin. The chars/4 heuristic portion is scaled by the factor; an explicit
1631:  * output reserve derived from the client's max_tokens (`routingReserveTokens`)
1632:  * is already an exact count and is added UNSCALED (#956 review). Trim-guarded
1633:  * platforms compare strictly — their guard guarantees the fit. */
1634: export function fitsContextWindow(platform: string, contextWindow: number | null | undefined, estimatedTokens: number, exactOutputReserve = 0): boolean {
1635:   if (contextWindow == null) return true;
1636:   // Raw advertised comparison first — the margin can only shrink eligibility.
1637:   if (estimatedTokens > contextWindow) return false;
1638:   if (TRIM_GUARDED_PLATFORMS.has(platform)) return true;
1639:   const reserve = Math.max(0, exactOutputReserve);
1640:   const heuristic = Math.max(0, estimatedTokens - reserve);
1641:   return heuristic * CONTEXT_WINDOW_SAFETY_FACTOR + reserve <= contextWindow;
1642: }
1643: 
1644: /**
1645:  * Route to ONE specific model, hard-pinned. Rotates across that model's keys
1646:  * (cooldowns, quotas, decryption all honored) but NEVER substitutes a different
1647:  * model — returns null if the pinned model can't serve right now. This is what
1648:  * makes a fusion panel genuinely diverse: a rate-limited slot is dropped, not
1649:  * silently collapsed onto whatever else is available. `skipKeys` lets a slot
1650:  * exclude keys it already failed on this request.
1651:  */
1652: export function routePinnedModel(modelDbId: number, estimatedTokens = 1000, skipKeys?: Set<string>): RouteResult | null {
1653:   const db = getDb();
1654:   const entry = getModelChainRow(db, modelDbId);
1655:   if (!entry) return null;
1656:   // Strict comparison only (#956 review): a pinned slot has no substitute, so
1657:   // refusing on a margin violation would drop the slot outright where the
1658:   // pre-margin behavior was one dispatch attempt (a mid-chain context_too_large
1659:   // 400 is classified and retried downstream). Nothing is multiplied here —
1660:   // estimatedTokens already carries the exact capped output reserve (#470).
1661:   if (!fitsContextWindowStrict(entry.context_window, estimatedTokens)) return null;
1662:   if (entry.tpm_limit != null && estimatedTokens > entry.tpm_limit) return null;
1663:   return selectKeyForModel(entry, estimatedTokens, skipKeys);
1664: }

1666: /**
1667:  * Resolve a logical model group's member db ids to an ordered ChainRow[] for
1668:  * strict group-pin routing (the "unify" feature). Each catalog-enabled member
1669:  * is hydrated as a ChainRow carrying its active-profile/manual priority, then
1670:  * ordered by the active strategy via orderChain. Auto-chain enabled/disabled is
1671:  * intentionally ignored here because an explicit model request should still be
1672:  * able to use a direct model that the user removed from auto routing.
1673:  *
1674:  * Pass the result to routeRequest() as `prefetchedChain` and DO NOT pass a
1675:  * `preferredModelDbId` that isn't already one of these rows — otherwise the
1676:  * preferred-model injection in routeRequest would unshift an off-group model and
1677:  * the pin would no longer be strict (it could answer with a different model).
1678:  */
1679: export function resolveModelGroupCandidates(
1680:   memberDbIds: number[],
1681:   /**
1682:    * Members that were reached only through a group's auto-derived slug, not the
1683:    * id the client wrote (#651). They stay in the chain — resolution must never
1684:    * shrink — but as a strictly lower tier, so they can serve only once every
1685:    * literal match is exhausted. Omit it and every row is an equal candidate,
1686:    * which is what every other caller wants.
1687:    */
1688:   demotedDbIds?: ReadonlySet<number>,
1689: ): ChainRow[] {
1690:   const db = getDb();
1691:   const strategy = getRoutingStrategy();
1692:   if (strategy !== 'priority') refreshStatsCache(db);
1693: 
1694:   const activeProfileId = getActiveProfileId(db);
1695:   const selectMember = activeProfileId == null
1696:     ? db.prepare(`
1697:       SELECT m.id as model_db_id, COALESCE(fc.priority, 0) as priority,
1698:              1 as enabled,
1699:              m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name, m.intelligence_rank,
1700:              m.size_label, m.monthly_token_budget,
1701:              m.rpm_limit, m.rpd_limit, m.tpm_limit, m.tpd_limit, m.supports_vision,
1702:              m.supports_tools, m.context_window, m.key_id, m.endpoint_scope
1703:       FROM models m
1704:       LEFT JOIN fallback_config fc ON fc.model_db_id = m.id
1705:       WHERE m.id = ? AND m.enabled = 1
1706:     `)
1707:     : db.prepare(`
1708:       SELECT m.id as model_db_id, COALESCE(pm.priority, fc.priority, 0) as priority,
1709:              1 as enabled,
1710:              m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name, m.intelligence_rank,
1711:              m.size_label, m.monthly_token_budget,
1712:              m.rpm_limit, m.rpd_limit, m.tpm_limit, m.tpd_limit, m.supports_vision,
1713:              m.supports_tools, m.context_window, m.key_id, m.endpoint_scope
1714:       FROM models m
1715:       LEFT JOIN profile_models pm ON pm.profile_id = ? AND pm.model_db_id = m.id
1716:       LEFT JOIN fallback_config fc ON fc.model_db_id = m.id
1717:       WHERE m.id = ? AND m.enabled = 1
1718:     `);
1719: 
1720:   const rows: ChainRow[] = [];
1721:   for (const id of memberDbIds) {
1722:     const row = (activeProfileId == null ? selectMember.get(id) : selectMember.get(activeProfileId, id)) as ChainRow | undefined;
1723:     if (!row) continue;
1724:     row.match_tier = demotedDbIds?.has(id) ? 1 : 0;
1725:     rows.push(row);
1726:   }
1727:   return orderChain(rows, strategy);
1728: }

1730: // A panel candidate surfaced to the fusion layer: enough to pick a diverse set
1731: // and resolve each to a pinned dispatch.
1732: export interface FusionCandidate {
1733:   modelDbId: number;
1734:   platform: string;
1735:   modelId: string;
1736:   displayName: string;
1737:   sizeLabel: string;
1738:   supportsVision: number;
1739:   supportsTools: number;
1740: }

1742: /**
1743:  * The active fallback chain ordered by the current routing strategy, surfaced
1744:  * for fusion panel selection. Same ordering the normal auto-router would walk,
1745:  * so the panel's auto-pick draws from the highest-scored models first and the
1746:  * fusion layer just needs to apply provider-diversity on top.
1747:  */
1748: export function getOrderedFusionChain(estimatedTokens: number, exactOutputReserve = 0): FusionCandidate[] {
1749:   const db = getDb();
1750:   const strategy = getRoutingStrategy();
1751:   if (strategy !== 'priority') refreshStatsCache(db);
1752:   const chain = getActiveChain(db).filter(e => e.enabled);
1753: 
1754:   // Only consider models that can ACTUALLY be served RIGHT NOW — applying the
1755:   // same gate selectKeyForModel uses when the router walks the chain: the model
1756:   // must have a key that is enabled + healthy, NOT on cooldown (e.g. a
1757:   // HuggingFace key benched for a day after a 402 "Payment Required"), within
1758:   // the provider's daily request cap, and under its per-minute/day request
1759:   // limits. Without this, a high-strategy-ranked model whose only key is
1760:   // currently cooled down (huggingface/Kimi-K2.6) would claim a panel slot it
1761:   // can't fill — surfacing as "no available key" and pushing out a usable model,
1762:   // which also makes the panel look like it's ignoring the routing strategy.
1763:   //
1764:   // The SIZE gates matter as much as the key gates: a model whose context window
1765:   // cannot hold the prompt can NEVER fill its slot, yet diversifyChain keeps
1766:   // handing it one on every request when it is its platform's only representative.
1767:   // That leaves one panel slot dead on arrival and reports the failure as the
1768:   // misleading "no available key for model". Passing a placeholder token count
1769:   // here made both size gates no-ops.
1770:   const usableKeys = db.prepare(
1771:     "SELECT id, platform, model_scope_json FROM api_keys WHERE enabled = 1 AND status IN ('healthy', 'unknown')"
1772:   ).all() as { id: number; platform: string; model_scope_json: string | null }[];
1773:   // Scope parsed once per key row (#657); the servable filter below re-checks
1774:   // membership per model.
1775:   const keysByPlatform = new Map<string, { id: number; scope: Set<string> | null }[]>();
1776:   for (const k of usableKeys) {
1777:     const entry = { id: k.id, scope: parseModelScope(k.model_scope_json) };
1778:     const arr = keysByPlatform.get(k.platform);
1779:     if (arr) arr.push(entry); else keysByPlatform.set(k.platform, [entry]);
1780:   }
1781:   // Soft preference (#956 review): prefer models whose window holds the estimate
1782:   // WITH the safety margin; /v1/models still advertises the raw window, so if
1783:   // NOTHING survives that pass, re-run allowing raw advertised-window fits
1784:   // rather than handing back an empty chain — a request packed to the
1785:   // advertised window keeps its one attempt (the mid-chain context_too_large
1786:   // 400 is classified and retried downstream).
1787:   const passesContextGate = (e: ChainRow, allowMarginViolators: boolean) => {
1788:     // A null context_window means "unknown", not "zero": same convention the
1789:     // auto-router uses, so an unspecified window is never itself a reason to skip.
1790:     if (fitsContextWindow(e.platform, e.context_window, estimatedTokens, exactOutputReserve)) return true;
1791:     return allowMarginViolators && fitsContextWindowStrict(e.context_window, estimatedTokens);
1792:   };
1793:   const servableFilter = (allowMarginViolators: boolean) => chain.filter(e => {
1794:     if (!passesContextGate(e, allowMarginViolators)) return false;
1795:     const keyIds = keysByPlatform.get(e.platform);
1796:     if (!keyIds) return false;
1797:     // Same endpoint-pool rule the router applies (#619).
1798:     const endpointKeyIds = e.platform === 'custom' && e.key_id != null
1799:       ? customEndpointKeyIds(db, e.key_id)
1800:       : null;
1801:     const limits = { rpm: e.rpm_limit, rpd: e.rpd_limit, tpm: e.tpm_limit, tpd: e.tpd_limit };
1802:     return keyIds.some(({ id: kid, scope }) =>
1803:       scopeAllows(scope, e.model_id) &&
1804:       (endpointKeyIds == null || endpointKeyIds.has(kid)) &&
1805:       !isOnCooldown(e.platform, e.model_id, kid) &&
1806:       canUseProvider(e.platform, kid) &&
1807:       canUseProviderMinute(e.platform, kid) &&
1808:       canMakeRequest(e.platform, e.model_id, kid, limits) &&
1809:       canUseProviderTokens(e.platform, kid, e.model_id, estimatedTokens),
1810:     );
1811:   });
1812:   let servable = servableFilter(false);
1813:   if (servable.length === 0) servable = servableFilter(true);
1814: 
1815:   // Deterministic (expected-score) ordering so the panel faithfully follows the
1816:   // user's picked routing strategy instead of re-sampling a fresh draw each call.
1817:   const ordered = orderChain(servable, strategy, false);
1818:   return ordered.map(e => ({
1819:     modelDbId: e.model_db_id,
1820:     platform: e.platform,
1821:     modelId: e.model_id,
1822:     displayName: e.display_name,
1823:     sizeLabel: e.size_label,
1824:     supportsVision: e.supports_vision,
1825:     supportsTools: e.supports_tools,
1826:   }));
1827: }

1829: /**
1830:  * Resolve an explicit model id (as a client would type it) to a fusion
1831:  * candidate, or null when it isn't a known enabled model. Prefers an enabled
1832:  * row; dedupes a model id that exists on multiple platforms by intelligence
1833:  * rank, matching how /v1/models picks a representative row.
1834:  */
1835: export function resolveFusionCandidate(modelId: string): FusionCandidate | null {
1836:   const db = getDb();
1837:   const row = db.prepare(`
1838:     SELECT m.id as model_db_id, m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name,
1839:            m.size_label, m.supports_vision, m.supports_tools
1840:     FROM models m
1841:     WHERE m.model_id = ? AND m.enabled = 1
1842:     ORDER BY m.intelligence_rank ASC, m.id ASC
1843:     LIMIT 1
1844:   `).get(modelId) as {
1845:     model_db_id: number; platform: string; model_id: string; display_name: string;
1846:     size_label: string; supports_vision: number; supports_tools: number;
1847:   } | undefined;
1848:   if (row) {
1849:     return {
1850:       modelDbId: row.model_db_id,
1851:       platform: row.platform,
1852:       modelId: row.model_id,
1853:       displayName: row.display_name,
1854:       sizeLabel: row.size_label,
1855:       supportsVision: row.supports_vision,
1856:       supportsTools: row.supports_tools,
1857:     };
1858:   }
1859: 
1860:   // Unify ON: a fusion picker value may be a canonical GROUP id rather than a
1861:   // raw model_id. Resolve it to the group's best-ordered enabled member so
1862:   // saved fusion configs that use canonical ids keep working. Exact model_id
1863:   // match above always wins first, so OFF mode and legacy configs are untouched.
1864:   if (isUnifyEnabled()) {
1865:     const resolved = resolveRequestedIdForDispatch(modelId, getModelGroups());
1866:     if (resolved && resolved.memberDbIds.length > 0) {
1867:       const top = resolveModelGroupCandidates(resolved.memberDbIds, resolved.demotedDbIds)[0];
1868:       if (top) {
1869:         return {
1870:           modelDbId: top.model_db_id,
1871:           platform: top.platform,
1872:           modelId: top.model_id,
1873:           displayName: top.display_name,
1874:           sizeLabel: top.size_label,
1875:           supportsVision: top.supports_vision,
1876:           supportsTools: top.supports_tools,
1877:         };
1878:       }
1879:     }
1880:   }
1881:   return null;
1882: }

1884: export function routeRequest(estimatedTokens = 1000, skipKeys?: Set<string>, preferredModelDbId?: number, requireVision = false, requireTools = false, skipModels?: Set<number>, prefetchedChain?: ChainRow[], requireStructured = false, skipPlatforms?: Set<string>, exactOutputReserve = 0): RouteResult {
1885:   const db = getDb();
1886: 
1887:   const strategy = getRoutingStrategy();
1888:   if (strategy !== 'priority') refreshStatsCache(db);
1889: 
1890:   const chain = (prefetchedChain ?? getActiveChain(db)).filter(e => e.enabled);
1891: 
1892:   const sortedChain = orderChain(chain, strategy);
1893: 
1894:   // Exploration toggle (#685/#707 follow-up): when enabled, give a model with
1895:   // no reliability/speed samples a guaranteed chance to be tried, so it stops
1896:   // losing every bandit draw to prior-heavy rivals. With EXPLORE_CHANCE
1897:   // probability, pick one unmeasured model uniformly and try it first; if it
1898:   // fails, the loop falls through to the scored order as usual. Only for
1899:   // bandit strategies — Manual is the operator's explicit order.
1900:   // Candidates the main loop would immediately reject for THIS request are
1901:   // excluded up front (ruled-out models plus the request-level capability
1902:   // gates: vision/tools/structured output/context window): promoting a model
1903:   // that can't serve the request ahead of capable ones would just get it
1904:   // skipped a moment later (e.g. an image request must never randomly probe a
1905:   // text-only model).
1906:   // While the gateway is in degraded mode (#904) exploration is skipped
1907:   // entirely: probing unmeasured models during a fleet-wide outage just burns
1908:   // retry budget on the same dead providers, and the scored order of known
1909:   // survivors is the only thing worth trying.
1910:   if (strategy !== 'priority' && getExploreEnabled() && !isDegraded() && Math.random() < EXPLORE_CHANCE) {
1911:     // A model the operator zeroed out via MODEL_ROUTING_OVERRIDES never wins a
1912:     // bandit draw, so it would stay under EXPLORE_MIN_SAMPLES forever and become
1913:     // a perpetual probe target — the explicit ban outranks exploration.
1914:     const overrides = getModelWeightOverrides();
1915:     const unmeasured = sortedChain.filter(e => {
1916:       if (overrides.get(e.model_id) === 0) return false;
1917:       const stats = statsCache?.get(modelStatsKey(e.platform, e.model_id, e.endpoint_scope));
1918:       if ((stats?.successes ?? 0) + (stats?.failures ?? 0) >= EXPLORE_MIN_SAMPLES) return false;
1919:       // Mirror the main loop's gates below so exploration only samples
1920:       // candidates that can actually serve this request.
1921:       if (skipModels?.has(e.model_db_id)) return false;
1922:       if (skipPlatforms?.has(e.platform)) return false;
1923:       if (requireVision && !e.supports_vision) return false;
1924:       if (requireTools && !e.supports_tools) return false;
1925:       if (requireStructured && platformDropsResponseFormat(e.platform)) return false;
1926:       if (!fitsContextWindow(e.platform, e.context_window, estimatedTokens, exactOutputReserve)) return false;
1927:       if (e.tpm_limit != null && estimatedTokens > e.tpm_limit) return false;
1928:       return true;
1929:     });
1930:     if (unmeasured.length > 0) {
1931:       const probe = unmeasured[Math.floor(Math.random() * unmeasured.length)];
1932:       const idx = sortedChain.findIndex(e => e.model_db_id === probe.model_db_id);
1933:       if (idx > 0) {
1934:         const [probeRow] = sortedChain.splice(idx, 1);
1935:         sortedChain.unshift(probeRow);
1936:       }
1937:     }
1938:   }
1939: 
1940:   // Sticky session / Explicit pinning: move preferred model to front of chain
1941:   if (preferredModelDbId) {
1942:     const idx = sortedChain.findIndex(e => e.model_db_id === preferredModelDbId);
1943:     if (idx >= 0) {
1944:       if (idx > 0) {
1945:         const [preferred] = sortedChain.splice(idx, 1);
1946:         sortedChain.unshift(preferred);
1947:       }
1948:     } else {
1949:       // The requested model is not in the current routing chain (e.g. it's a
1950:       // custom model or not added to the active profile). We must fulfill the
1951:       // explicit request by injecting it at the front.
1952:       const pinnedRow = db.prepare(`
1953:         SELECT m.id as model_db_id, 0 as priority, 1 as enabled,
1954:                m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name, m.intelligence_rank,
1955:                m.size_label, m.monthly_token_budget,
1956:                m.rpm_limit, m.rpd_limit, m.tpm_limit, m.tpd_limit, m.supports_vision,
1957:                m.supports_tools, m.context_window, m.key_id, m.endpoint_scope
1958:         FROM models m
1959:         WHERE m.id = ? AND m.enabled = 1
1960:       `).get(preferredModelDbId) as ChainRow | undefined;
1961:       
1962:       if (pinnedRow) {
1963:         sortedChain.unshift(pinnedRow);
1964:       }
1965:     }
1966:   }
1967: 
1968:   // Per-model disposition, attached to the exhaustion error when the loop falls
1969:   // through with no route — the only record of WHY the pool was empty on the
1970:   // synchronous "all exhausted" path (nothing downstream logs it). See issue _1.
1971:   const diag: string[] = [];
1972: 
1973:   // Margin as a SOFT preference (#956 review): /v1/models advertises the raw
1974:   // window, so clients legitimately pack requests right up to it — excluding
1975:   // those models outright turned an already-handled upstream 400 into "all
1976:   // models exhausted" with zero attempts. Keep the operator's order intact but
1977:   // sweep margin-fitting models first; ones that only fit the advertised window
1978:   // stay eligible behind them. Worst case is one classified context_too_large
1979:   // hop instead of no route at all.
1980:   const servingChain: ChainRow[] = [];
1981:   const marginDeferred: ChainRow[] = [];
1982:   for (const e of sortedChain) {
1983:     (fitsContextWindow(e.platform, e.context_window, estimatedTokens, exactOutputReserve) ? servingChain : marginDeferred).push(e);
1984:   }
1985:   servingChain.push(...marginDeferred);
1986: 
1987:   for (const entry of servingChain) {
1988:     const label = `${entry.platform}/${entry.model_id}`;
1989:     // Models the caller has ruled out for this request — e.g. a 404
1990:     // "model removed upstream" already seen this request: trying the same
1991:     // model again on a different key would just burn another attempt on the
1992:     // same dead route (PR #111, credits @barbotkonv).
1993:     if (skipModels?.has(entry.model_db_id)) { diag.push(`${label}: ruled out earlier this request`); continue; }
1994: 
1995:     // Platforms the caller has ruled out wholesale (#788): a provider-level
1996:     // failure this request — a 5xx, a timeout, a dead socket — is about the
1997:     // PROVIDER, so its other keys and its other models would fail the same way.
1998:     // Skipping the platform moves failover to the next provider instead of
1999:     // burning one hop per key. Request-scoped; nothing is benched by this.
2000:     if (skipPlatforms?.has(entry.platform)) { diag.push(`${label}: provider ruled out earlier this request`); continue; }
2001: 
2002:     // Vision requests skip text-only models — including a sticky/preferred one,
2003:     // which is correct: don't pin an image turn to a model that can't see it.
2004:     if (requireVision && !entry.supports_vision) { diag.push(`${label}: no vision support`); continue; }
2005: 
2006:     // Tool-bearing requests skip models that can't emit structured tool_calls.
2007:     // A model that "answers" a tool request with the call serialized as text
2008:     // looks successful at the transport level while the client's harness sees
2009:     // nothing — worse than a failover. Applies to sticky models too, same
2010:     // reasoning as vision above.
2011:     if (requireTools && !entry.supports_tools) { diag.push(`${label}: no tool-calling support`); continue; }
2012: 
2013:     // Structured-output routing (#514 follow-up): when the request carries a
2014:     // response_format, skip platforms whose param policy can't even receive it
2015:     // (the param would be dropped before send, so the model would answer in
2016:     // prose and burn a failover hop). Platform-level fast path — model-level
2017:     // capability isn't in the catalog; models that accept the param but ignore
2018:     // it are caught by the non-stream JSON enforcement downstream.
2019:     if (requireStructured && platformDropsResponseFormat(entry.platform)) { diag.push(`${label}: platform drops response_format`); continue; }

32: // Append a row to the request analytics table. Shared by the chat proxy, the
33: // responses path, and the fusion panel so every served (or failed) sub-request
34: // is logged identically. Lives in a neutral lib module to avoid an import cycle
35: // between the fusion service and the proxy route that both call it.
36: //
37: // Status is 'success', 'error', or 'canceled' (#752 — the client hung up
38: // mid-attempt). A canceled request counts toward request totals — it happened —
39: // but toward NEITHER success nor error: rates and scoring must read
40: // success/(success+error), never success/total.
41: //
42: // In addition to the raw row, we update two durable aggregates so analytics
43: // totals survive the raw-row prune (REQUEST_ANALYTICS_MAX_ROWS):
44: //   - request_hourly: per-hour bucket counts and tokens (max window = 30d).
45: //   - settings: lifetime totals (total_requests, total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens)
46: //     plus first_request_at (set on the first ever logged request).
47: // All upserts run in the same transaction so the aggregates never disagree
48: // with the raw row count.
49: export function logRequest(
50:   platform: string,
51:   modelId: string,
52:   // NULL for rejections that never reached routing (no key was involved),
53:   // e.g. an over-limit request body turned away at the parser.
54:   keyId: number | null,
55:   status: string,
56:   inputTokens: number,
57:   outputTokens: number,
58:   latencyMs: number,
59:   error: string | null,
60:   ttfbMs: number | null = null,
61:   // The model id the client pinned; null for auto-routed requests. Lets
62:   // analytics split pinned vs auto traffic and detect failover overrides
63:   // (requested_model set but != model_id).
64:   requestedModel: string | null = null,
65:   // The model the UPSTREAM claims it served, ONLY when it genuinely differs
66:   // from the routed model_id after cosmetic normalization (#534 — see
67:   // lib/served-model.ts). NULL when it matches or the provider reported
68:   // nothing usable, so the column stays empty in the healthy case.
69:   servedModel: string | null = null,
70: ) {
71:   try {
72:     const db = getDb();
73:     // Caller identity from the request-scoped context (set by the express
74:     // middleware); null when logging happens outside an HTTP request.
75:     const client = getClientContext();
76:     const tx = db.transaction(() => {
77:       const insert = db.prepare(`
78:         INSERT INTO requests (platform, model_id, key_id, status, input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_ms, error, ttfb_ms, requested_model, served_model, client_ip, client_user_agent, client_agent)
79:         VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
80:       `).run(platform, modelId, keyId, status, inputTokens, outputTokens, latencyMs, error, ttfbMs, requestedModel, servedModel, client.ip, client.userAgent, client.agent);
81: 
82:       // Report the row id back to the fallback loop's attempt trace (if one is
83:       // active): the LAST id noted during a loop run is the terminal row the

85:       if (insert.lastInsertRowid != null) noteRequestRowId(insert.lastInsertRowid);

88:       const hour = hourKey(createdAt?.created_at ?? new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 19).replace('T', ' '));
89:       const isSuccess = status === 'success' ? 1 : 0;
90:       const isError = status === 'error' ? 1 : 0;
91: 
92:       db.prepare(`
93:         INSERT INTO request_hourly (hour, total_requests, success_count, error_count, input_tokens, output_tokens)
94:         VALUES (?, 1, ?, ?, ?, ?)
95:         ON CONFLICT(hour) DO UPDATE SET
96:           total_requests = total_requests + 1,
97:           success_count  = success_count + ?,
98:           error_count    = error_count + ?,
99:           input_tokens   = input_tokens + ?,
100:           output_tokens  = output_tokens + ?
101:       `).run(hour, isSuccess, isError, inputTokens, outputTokens, isSuccess, isError, inputTokens, outputTokens);
102: 
103:       incrementSetting(db, 'total_requests', 1);
104:       incrementSetting(db, 'total_input_tokens', inputTokens);
105:       incrementSetting(db, 'total_output_tokens', outputTokens);
106:       if (createdAt?.created_at) {
107:         setSettingIfMissing(db, 'first_request_at', createdAt.created_at);
108:       }
109:     });
110:     tx();
111: 
112:     pruneRequestAnalytics({ db });
113:   } catch (e) {
114:     console.error('Failed to log request:', e);
115:   }
116: }
117: 
118: // Persist a finished attempt trace as one small insert batch keyed to the
119: // terminal `requests` row of the failover ladder (the success row, a committed
120: // mid-stream error row, or the last per-attempt failure row). Called once per
121: // request by the fallback loop AFTER the response is finished, so the write is
122: // off the client's latency path. Zero-failure single-attempt successes write
123: // exactly one 'ok' row. A trace with no parent row writes nothing — since the
124: // fallback loop logs a 'canceled' row for pure client aborts (#752), that is
125: // now only the loop-top stop paths, whose failed attempts each wrote their own
126: // row already.
127: export function persistRequestAttempts(trace: RequestTrace): void {
128:   if (trace.records.length === 0 || trace.lastRequestRowId == null) return;
129:   try {
130:     const db = getDb();
131:     const insert = db.prepare(`
132:       INSERT INTO request_attempts (request_id, ordinal, platform, model_id, key_ordinal, key_label, outcome, start_offset_ms, duration_ms, error_summary)
133:       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
134:     `);
135:     const tx = db.transaction(() => {
136:       for (const r of trace.records) {
137:         insert.run(trace.lastRequestRowId, r.ordinal, r.platform, r.modelId, r.keyOrdinal, r.keyLabel, r.outcome, r.startOffsetMs, r.durationMs, r.errorSummary);
138:       }
139:     });
140:     tx();
141:   } catch (e) {
142:     console.error('Failed to persist request attempts:', e);
143:   }
144: }

1: import { Router } from 'express';
2: import type { Request, Response } from 'express';
3: import { getDb } from '../db/index.js';
4: import { checkKeyHealth, checkAllKeys } from '../services/health.js';
5: import { getDegradationStatus } from '../services/degradation.js';
6: import { hasProvider } from '../providers/index.js';
7: import { getQuotaStateForKeys } from '../services/provider-quota.js';
8: 
9: export const healthRouter = Router();
10: 
11: // Get health status for all platforms
12: healthRouter.get('/', (_req: Request, res: Response) => {
13:   const db = getDb();
14: 
15:   const platforms = db.prepare(`
16:     SELECT
17:       platform,
18:       COUNT(*) as total_keys,
19:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'healthy' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as healthy_keys,
20:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'rate_limited' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as rate_limited_keys,
21:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'invalid' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as invalid_keys,
22:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as error_keys,
23:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'unknown' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as unknown_keys,
24:       SUM(CASE WHEN enabled = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as enabled_keys
25:     FROM api_keys
26:     GROUP BY platform
27:   `).all() as any[];
28: 
29:   const keys = db.prepare(`
30:     SELECT id, platform, label, status, enabled, created_at, last_checked_at, last_health_error
31:     FROM api_keys
32:     ORDER BY platform, created_at DESC
33:   `).all() as any[];
34: 
35:   res.json({
36:     platforms: platforms.map(p => ({
37:       platform: p.platform,
38:       hasProvider: hasProvider(p.platform),
39:       totalKeys: p.total_keys,
40:       healthyKeys: p.healthy_keys,
41:       rateLimitedKeys: p.rate_limited_keys,
42:       invalidKeys: p.invalid_keys,
43:       errorKeys: p.error_keys,
44:       unknownKeys: p.unknown_keys,
45:       enabledKeys: p.enabled_keys,
46:     })),
47:     keys: keys.map(k => ({
48:       id: k.id,
49:       platform: k.platform,
50:       label: k.label,
51:       status: k.status,
52:       enabled: k.enabled === 1,
53:       createdAt: k.created_at,
54:       lastCheckedAt: k.last_checked_at,
55:       lastHealthError: k.last_health_error,
56:     })),
57:     quotaStates: getQuotaStateForKeys(),
58:     degradation: getDegradationStatus(),
59:   });
60: });
61: 
62: // Check a specific key
63: healthRouter.post('/check/:keyId', async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
64:   const keyId = parseInt(req.params.keyId as string, 10);
65:   if (isNaN(keyId)) {
66:     res.status(400).json({ error: { message: 'Invalid key ID' } });
67:     return;
68:   }
69: 
70:   const status = await checkKeyHealth(keyId);
71:   res.json({ keyId, status });
72: });
73: 
74: // Check all keys. Forced: someone pressed the button and wants an answer about
75: // every key now, so the scheduled pass' recency skip and provider spacing (#553)
76: // don't apply.
77: healthRouter.post('/check-all', async (_req: Request, res: Response) => {
78:   await checkAllKeys({ force: true });
79:   res.json({ success: true });
80: });

TOKEN="e6df3fd981f545a60ad3cb60c64ebc2e938e944252e0c13e33a7af738b9037d1"
timeout 20 curl -s -N "http://localhost:3010/api/sse/monitor" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" > /tmp/sse-monitor.log 2>&1 &
SSE_PID=$!
echo "SSE PID: $SSE_PID"
sleep 2

# Check that SSE subscribed to redis
echo "--- Redis channels (after SSE connect) ---"
docker exec jimesh-redis redis-cli pubsub channels 2>&1
echo "--- Redis numsub ---"
docker exec jimesh-redis redis-cli pubsub numsub jimesh:routing:scores jimesh:routing:decision jimesh:routing:failure jimesh:key:cooldown jimesh:requests 2>&1

# Wait for SSE to finish
wait $SSE_PID 2>/dev/null
echo "--- SSE Monitor output ---"
cat /tmp/sse-monitor.log","description":"Verify SSE subscribes to Redis channels"}
