<type>file</type>
<content>
1: // ── Redis Pub/Sub for real-time event broadcasting ──────────────────────────
2: // Singleton ioredis client + subscriber. The server's existing SSE routes still
3: // work via the in-process `clients` Set, but instead of polling the SQLite DB
4: // every 2-5 seconds they now receive every event as it happens through
5: // Pub/Sub, mirroring the trading bot's realtime pattern.
6: //
7: // Channels (all under the `jimesh:` namespace to avoid clashing with anything
8: // else on a shared Redis instance):
9: //   jimesh:routing:scores   — periodic model score snapshots (analytics feed)
10: //   jimesh:routing:decision — every successful routing decision (model+key+ms)
11: //   jimesh:routing:failure  — every model that failed on a request (no key, 429,
12: //                              upstream 5xx, cooldown, context too large, ...)
13: //   jimesh:key:cooldown     — every time a key is put on cooldown
14: //   jimesh:requests         — every request that completed (status, latency,
15: //                              input/output tokens) for the realtime monitor
16: //
17: // Graceful degradation: if Redis is unavailable at boot, every publish/subscribe
18: // call is a no-op. The rest of the server continues to function (SSE falls back
19: // to its existing in-process clients). The client reconnect logic takes care of
20: // recovering once Redis is back up — no manual restart required.
21: 
22: import IORedis, { type Redis as RedisClient, type RedisOptions } from 'ioredis';
23: 
24: // Channels we publish on. Kept here so producers and the SSE bridge import the
25: // exact same strings and never silently disagree.
26: export const CHANNEL = {
27:   ROUTING_SCORES: 'jimesh:routing:scores',
28:   ROUTING_DECISION: 'jimesh:routing:decision',
29:   ROUTING_FAILURE: 'jimesh:routing:failure',
30:   KEY_COOLDOWN: 'jimesh:key:cooldown',
31:   REQUESTS: 'jimesh:requests',
32: } as const;
33: 
34: export type ChannelName = (typeof CHANNEL)[keyof typeof CHANNEL];
35: 
36: // Is the Pub/Sub layer wired up? Checked by callers that want to fail-safe
37: // without paying the cost of a try/catch on every publish.
38: let enabled = false;
39: 
40: // Status flag updated by the ioredis 'ready' / 'end' / 'error' events so other
41: // modules can show a connection indicator in the dashboard without re-running
42: // the connect logic.
43: let connected = false;
44: 
45: // Parsed once at boot. REDIS_ENABLED=false short-circuits the whole module so
46: // installs that don't have or don't want Redis (single-user localhost setups)
47: // can keep working unchanged.
48: function readConfig(): { url: string; enabled: boolean } {
49:   const url = process.env.REDIS_URL || 'redis://127.0.0.1:6379';
50:   const enabled = (process.env.REDIS_ENABLED ?? 'true').toLowerCase() !== 'false';
51:   return { url, enabled };
52: }
53: 
54: // Shared client options. Retry strategy caps the backoff at 2s so a Redis
55: // outage that recovers later doesn't keep the server waiting on an exponential
56: // delay curve.
57: function buildOptions(): RedisOptions {
58:   return {
59:     // Don't blow up boot if Redis is offline — ioredis queues commands and
60:     // reconnects in the background. The 'ready' / 'end' handlers flip the
61:     // `connected` flag so the rest of the app can react.
62:     enableOfflineQueue: true,
63:     maxRetriesPerRequest: 3,
64:     // Cap the reconnect backoff so a long Redis outage doesn't put us out for
65:     // minutes when it finally comes back.
66:     retryStrategy: (times) => Math.min(times * 200, 2000),
67:     // Don't print "ready" / "connect" / "error" on every reconnect — the
68:     // logger already records them, and ioredis's default is noisy.
69:     lazyConnect: false,
70:   };
71: }
72: 
73: let publisher: RedisClient | null = null;
74: let subscriber: RedisClient | null = null;
75: 
76: /**
77:  * Wire up the publisher and subscriber. Idempotent: a second call is a no-op
78:  * so it's safe to invoke from both index.ts (at boot) and any future hot-reload
79:  * path. Disables itself and returns gracefully if REDIS_ENABLED=false or the
80:  * initial connect fails — every publish then becomes a fire-and-forget no-op.
81:  */
82: export function initRedis(): void {
83:   if (publisher && subscriber) return; // already wired
84:   const { url, enabled: cfgEnabled } = readConfig();
85:   if (!cfgEnabled) {
86:     console.log('[redis] REDIS_ENABLED=false — Pub/Sub disabled, SSE stays in-process');
87:     enabled = false;
88:     return;
89:   }
90: 
91:   enabled = true;
92:   try {
93:     publisher = new IORedis(url, buildOptions());
94:     subscriber = new IORedis(url, buildOptions());
95: 
96:     publisher.on('ready', () => {
97:       connected = true;
98:       console.log(`[redis] publisher ready (${url})`);
99:     });
100:     publisher.on('end', () => {
101:       connected = false;
102:       console.warn('[redis] publisher connection ended — will retry');
103:     });
104:     publisher.on('error', (err) => {
105:       // Suppress "ECONNREFUSED" spam when Redis is simply not running on the
106:       // local dev box — ioredis retries on its own.
107:       if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException)?.code !== 'ECONNREFUSED') {
108:         console.warn(`[redis] publisher error: ${err.message}`);
109:       }
110:     });
111: 
112:     subscriber.on('ready', () => {
113:       console.log(`[redis] subscriber ready (${url})`);
114:     });
115:     subscriber.on('end', () => {
116:       console.warn('[redis] subscriber connection ended — will retry');
117:     });
118:     subscriber.on('error', (err) => {
119:       if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException)?.code !== 'ECONNREFUSED') {
120:         console.warn(`[redis] subscriber error: ${err.message}`);
121:       }
122:     });
123:   } catch (err: any) {
124:     // A misformed REDIS_URL throws synchronously out of new IORedis(). Treat
125:     // it the same as a refused connection: log once and continue in disabled
126:     // mode.
127:     console.warn(`[redis] failed to initialise — Pub/Sub disabled: ${err?.message ?? err}`);
128:     publisher = null;
129:     subscriber = null;
130:     enabled = false;
131:   }
132: }
133: 
134: /**
135:  * Stop the Pub/Sub client cleanly. Used by the server's shutdown handler so
